title: TableAI Catalog
summary: A reviewed directory of AI applications, skills, agents, benchmarks, and technical writing.
description: This repository's catalog-first public experience, built as static Astro pages with a Cloudflare Worker API and operations layer.

showcase.problem: AI tooling is fragmented across repositories, publications, and product directories.
showcase.architecture: Astro static generation, schema-validated Git content, and a Cloudflare Worker for public and operational APIs.

title: cfker01 Operations Worker
summary: A Cloudflare management Worker for health, status aggregation, audit events, API keys, and MCP access.
description: The operational subsystem retained by this catalog, with scheduled provider checks, D1 history, KV snapshots, protected administration, and structured logs.

showcase.problem: Cloud operations checks and AI provider status were spread across manual tools.
showcase.architecture: Worker fetch and cron handlers backed by D1, KV, provider collectors, API keys, and an MCP endpoint.

title: OpenAI Codex
summary: A coding agent for software development tasks across local tools, repositories, and cloud workflows.
description: Codex supports repository exploration, implementation, testing, review, and collaboration through coding-focused agent surfaces.

title: Claude Code
summary: An agentic coding tool that works from the terminal and integrates with development workflows.
description: Claude Code reads codebases, edits files, runs commands, and supports automation through terminal-centered agent workflows.

title: Aider
summary: An open-source pair programming agent designed to edit code in local Git repositories.
description: Aider connects language models to local repositories, supports multi-file changes, and integrates edits with Git workflows.

title: Cline
summary: An open-source coding agent that operates inside Visual Studio Code with user-approved tool actions.
description: Cline can inspect projects, edit files, execute terminal commands, and interact with browsers through an approval-oriented interface.

title: Continue
summary: An open-source platform for building and using AI coding assistants in developer environments.
description: Continue provides IDE integrations and configurable model, context, rule, and agent components for coding workflows.

title: OpenHands
summary: An open-source platform for software development agents that work through code, terminals, and browsers.
description: OpenHands provides agent runtimes, evaluation tooling, and interfaces for delegating software engineering tasks.

title: SWE-agent
summary: A research system that enables language models to resolve software engineering tasks in repositories.
description: SWE-agent supplies an agent-computer interface and evaluation workflow for issue-driven software engineering experiments.

title: SWE-bench
summary: A benchmark for evaluating language models on real software engineering issues from open-source repositories.
description: SWE-bench pairs GitHub issues with repository snapshots and tests to measure whether generated patches resolve real tasks.

benchmarkEvidence.limitations: Results depend on the benchmark variant, execution environment, and submission policy.

title: Terminal-Bench
summary: A benchmark for measuring AI agents on practical tasks completed in terminal environments.
description: Terminal-Bench defines containerized terminal tasks and evaluation infrastructure for reproducible agent comparisons.

benchmarkEvidence.limitations: Scores are specific to task set, harness version, model access, and agent configuration.

title: AgentBench
summary: A benchmark suite designed to evaluate language models acting as agents across varied environments.
description: AgentBench covers interactive tasks spanning operating systems, databases, knowledge graphs, games, and web environments.

benchmarkEvidence.evaluatedTarget: Models reported by the benchmark authors
benchmarkEvidence.limitations: Reported results reflect the environments, prompts, and model versions used by the authors.

title: BrowserGym
summary: A framework and benchmark family for evaluating web agents in browser-based environments.
description: BrowserGym supplies unified browser observation and action spaces plus integrations with multiple web task benchmarks.

title: WebArena
summary: A realistic web environment for evaluating autonomous agents on reproducible tasks.
description: WebArena provides self-hostable websites, task definitions, and evaluation criteria for web navigation and interaction agents.

title: OSWorld
summary: A benchmark for multimodal agents that operate full computer environments through visual interaction.
description: OSWorld supplies real operating-system tasks, virtual machine environments, and execution-based evaluation for computer-use agents.

title: Inspect AI
summary: An open-source framework for building and running language-model evaluations.
description: Inspect AI provides datasets, solvers, tools, scorers, logs, and sandbox support for reproducible model evaluations.

title: OpenAI Evals
summary: An open-source framework and registry for evaluating language models and model systems.
description: OpenAI Evals supports evaluation definitions, data, model adapters, and reporting for testing model behavior.

title: LM Evaluation Harness
summary: A framework for evaluating language models across a broad collection of academic tasks.
description: The harness standardizes task definitions, model adapters, few-shot prompting, and metric calculation for model evaluation.

title: LangChain
summary: A framework and ecosystem for building applications that use language models, tools, retrieval, and agents.
description: LangChain provides composable libraries and integrations for agent loops, retrieval pipelines, tool use, and observability.

title: LangGraph
summary: A low-level orchestration framework for stateful, controllable agents and long-running workflows.
description: LangGraph models agent systems as graphs with explicit state, durable execution, streaming, memory, and human intervention.

title: Microsoft AutoGen
summary: A framework for creating agentic AI applications with single-agent and multi-agent patterns.
description: AutoGen provides layered APIs for event-driven agents, conversations, tools, model clients, and distributed runtimes.

title: CrewAI
summary: A framework for coordinating role-based AI agents, tasks, tools, and production workflows.
description: CrewAI supports autonomous crews and event-driven flows for building structured multi-agent applications.

title: Semantic Kernel
summary: A model integration SDK for building agents and AI applications in several programming languages.
description: Semantic Kernel connects models, plugins, memory, planners, and agent abstractions within conventional application architectures.

title: LlamaIndex
summary: A framework for connecting language-model applications and agents to private and external data.
description: LlamaIndex supplies data connectors, indexes, query engines, retrieval workflows, tools, and agent components.

title: Haystack
summary: An open-source framework for production retrieval, search, question-answering, and agent pipelines.
description: Haystack provides typed components, pipelines, document stores, model integrations, tools, and agent orchestration.

title: Pydantic AI
summary: A Python agent framework built around typed dependencies, structured outputs, tools, and model portability.
description: Pydantic AI applies Pydantic validation and dependency-injection patterns to production agent development.

title: OpenAI Agents SDK
summary: A lightweight SDK for agent loops, tools, handoffs, guardrails, sessions, and tracing.
description: The OpenAI Agents SDK offers Python and JavaScript primitives for composing tool-using agents and observable workflows.

title: Model Context Protocol Servers
summary: Reference implementations and community servers that expose tools and resources through MCP.
description: The MCP servers repository demonstrates integrations that let compatible AI applications access data sources and executable tools.

title: Agent Skills Specification
summary: An open format for packaging instructions and resources that agents can discover and apply.
description: Agent Skills defines a portable directory convention centered on SKILL.md instructions with optional scripts, references, and assets.

title: Browser Use
summary: An open-source library that connects AI agents to browser automation workflows.
description: Browser Use exposes browser state and actions to language-model agents and supports repeatable web automation tasks.

title: Playwright MCP
summary: An MCP server that gives agents structured browser automation through Playwright accessibility data.
description: Playwright MCP lets compatible agents navigate, inspect, and interact with web pages using deterministic browser tooling.

title: n8n
summary: A workflow automation platform with extensible integrations and AI-oriented nodes and agents.
description: n8n provides a visual workflow editor, execution engine, integrations, code steps, and self-hosting options.

title: Dify
summary: An open-source platform for composing, deploying, and operating language-model applications and agents.
description: Dify combines visual workflows, retrieval, model management, agent tools, observability, and application APIs.

title: Flowise
summary: An open-source visual platform for building language-model workflows and agent systems.
description: Flowise offers node-based orchestration, integrations, deployment APIs, and reusable flows for AI application development.

title: Langflow
summary: A visual framework for creating and serving AI workflows with reusable Python components.
description: Langflow provides a graph editor, component ecosystem, playground, and API deployment path for agent and retrieval flows.

title: Ollama
summary: A local runtime and command-line application for downloading and running language models.
description: Ollama packages model execution, model definitions, a local API, and cross-platform tooling for local model use.

title: Open WebUI
summary: A self-hosted web interface for interacting with local and remote language-model services.
description: Open WebUI provides conversations, model connections, retrieval, tools, administration, and extensible pipelines.

title: LiteLLM
summary: A model gateway and SDK that provides a consistent interface across many language-model providers.
description: LiteLLM supports provider translation, routing, fallbacks, budgets, logging, caching, and an OpenAI-compatible proxy.

title: Helicone
summary: An open-source observability platform for monitoring and analyzing language-model application traffic.
description: Helicone records model requests, costs, latency, sessions, evaluations, and experiments through gateway and integration options.

title: Langfuse
summary: An open-source platform for traces, prompt management, evaluations, metrics, and datasets for LLM applications.
description: Langfuse connects application telemetry with prompts, experiments, scores, and production analytics.

title: Arize Phoenix
summary: An open-source observability and evaluation platform for language-model and machine-learning applications.
description: Phoenix supports tracing, datasets, experiments, evaluators, embeddings analysis, and OpenTelemetry integrations.

title: Promptfoo
summary: An open-source command-line and web toolkit for testing prompts, models, agents, and red-team scenarios.
description: Promptfoo runs configurable evaluation matrices, assertions, comparisons, reports, and adversarial tests in CI or locally.

title: Ragas
summary: An open-source framework for evaluating retrieval-augmented generation systems and AI workflows.
description: Ragas provides evaluation metrics, experiment support, test data generation, and integrations for retrieval and agent pipelines.

title: DeepEval
summary: An open-source evaluation framework for testing language-model systems with metrics and datasets.
description: DeepEval supports model-graded metrics, retrieval and agent evaluations, synthetic data, red teaming, and CI integration.

title: Guardrails AI
summary: A framework and hub for validating, constraining, and monitoring language-model inputs and outputs.
description: Guardrails AI defines validators and structured generation patterns for enforcing application requirements around model behavior.

title: Instructor
summary: A library for obtaining validated structured outputs from language models using typed application schemas.
description: Instructor layers retries, validation, streaming, and provider adapters around typed model responses.

title: Gradio
summary: An open-source Python library for creating web interfaces and demos for machine-learning models.
description: Gradio turns Python functions into interactive web applications with reusable components, sharing, and deployment support.

title: Streamlit
summary: An open-source Python framework for rapidly building interactive data and AI applications.
description: Streamlit provides a reactive script model, interface components, data display, caching, and deployment workflows.
